title: Continuity on a quotient times a locally compact space
statement: Let $X_0,X,T,Z$ be topological spaces and let $q:X_0\to X$ be a quotient map: $q$ is surjective and a subset $U\subseteq X$ is open if and only if $q^{-1}(U)$ is open. Suppose $T$ is locally compact, meaning that every neighborhood of every point contains a compact neighborhood of that point; subsets carry the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Give the products their product topologies. For any function $H:X\times T\to Z$, if $(x_0,t)\mapsto H(q(x_0),t)$ is continuous on $X_0\times T$, then $H$ is continuous on $X\times T$.
